docs.title: VisionFI Policy Analyzer
docs.text:
Create Scout CEL rule bundles from policy documents inside the partner environment.

VisionFI Policy Analyzer is a .NET package for partners who do not work inside VisionFI CRM. A partner application sends consumer-lending policy PDFs or free-form policy text into the SDK, receives an evidence report and a staged CEL rule-bundle payload, and stores that payload for later Scout HQ integration.

Scout HQ provides the FI identity, authoring profile, schema artifacts, and provider credentials. Policy documents and policy text are not sent to Scout HQ.

docs.title: What It Produces
docs.text:
The SDK returns the same rule-bundle wrapper shape used by VisionFI CRM:

{
  "product_key": "consumer-qc",
  "workflow_key": "consumer-loan-qc",
  "version": "2026.06.03.1",
  "bundle_json": {
    "institution_id": "fi-123",
    "version": "2026.06.03.1",
    "product_id": "consumer-loan-qc",
    "rules": [],
    "derivations": [],
    "tables": {}
  },
  "active": false
}

The payload is staged output. A partner-owned approval and storage workflow decides when and how the bundle is later integrated with Scout HQ.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Partner .NET Application
  -> VisionFI Policy Analyzer
  -> Scout HQ using FI token
       - validates token
       - returns institution identity
       - returns authoring profile
       - returns provider credentials
  -> Local SDK authoring run
       - sends source material directly to managed inference
       - validates and shapes the CEL bundle
  -> Partner stores staged bundle
  1. The partner application provides an FI token issued by Scout HQ.
  2. The SDK retrieves a product/workflow-specific authoring profile from Scout HQ.
  3. The SDK sends PDFs or free-form policy text to managed inference from the partner environment.
  4. The SDK returns an evidence report and a CRM-compatible rule-bundle wrapper.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
using VisionFI.Scout.Authoring;

var client = new ScoutAuthoringClient(new ScoutAuthoringOptions
{
    HqBaseUrl = "https://scout-hq.example.com",
    ScoutToken = "<fi-token>"
});

var result = await client.AuthorRuleBundleAsync(new AuthorRuleBundleRequest
{
    ProfileKey = "consumer-qc.consumer-loan-qc.policy-cel-authoring",
    Version = "2026.06.03.1",
    Sources =
    [
        AuthoringSource.FromPdf("consumer-loan-policy.pdf"),
        AuthoringSource.FromText("loan-checklist.txt", checklistText)
    ]
});

Console.WriteLine(result.EvidenceReportMarkdown);
Console.WriteLine(result.RuleBundleWrapperJson);

Get started View architecture

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
This page documents the public surface for VisionFI Policy Analyzer.

The NuGet package ID is VisionFI.PolicyAnalyzer. The current public C# namespace is VisionFI.Scout.Authoring.

docs.title: ScoutAuthoringClient
docs.text:
Main entry point for rule-bundle authoring.

var client = new ScoutAuthoringClient(new ScoutAuthoringOptions
{
    HqBaseUrl = "https://scout-hq.example.com",
    ScoutToken = "<fi-token>"
});

docs.title: AuthorRuleBundleAsync
docs.text:
Task<AuthorRuleBundleResult> AuthorRuleBundleAsync(
    AuthorRuleBundleRequest request,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);

Authors a staged CEL rule bundle from PDF and text source material.

docs.title: ScoutAuthoringOptions
docs.text:
Property Type Description HqBaseUrl string Scout HQ base URL ScoutToken string FI token issued by Scout HQ HttpClient HttpClient? Optional caller-provided HTTP client

The token is sent to Scout HQ as:

X-Scout-Token: <fi-token>

docs.title: AuthorRuleBundleRequest
docs.text:
Property Type Description ProfileKey string Authoring profile key, for example consumer-qc.consumer-loan-qc.policy-cel-authoring Version string Bundle version, conventionally YYYY.MM.DD.N Sources IReadOnlyList<AuthoringSource> PDFs and free-form text used for authoring

The SDK enforces that wrapper version and nested bundle_json.version match this value.

docs.title: AuthoringSource
docs.text:
Represents source material supplied by the partner application.

var pdf = AuthoringSource.FromPdf("consumer-loan-policy.pdf");
var text = AuthoringSource.FromText("checklist.txt", checklistText);
Property Description FileName Display/source name MediaType application/pdf or text/plain Content Raw source bytes or text

docs.title: AuthorRuleBundleResult
docs.text: Property Description EvidenceReportMarkdown Source-grounded evidence report RuleBundleWrapperJson Serialized CRM-compatible wrapper RuleBundleWrapper Typed wrapper object Validation CEL compile and field-path validation status ProfileKey Profile used ProfileVersion Profile version used InputTokens / OutputTokens Provider token usage, when available

docs.title: RuleBundleWrapper
docs.text:
public sealed class RuleBundleWrapper
{
    public string ProductKey { get; init; }
    public string WorkflowKey { get; init; }
    public string Version { get; init; }
    public JsonElement BundleJson { get; init; }
    public bool Active { get; init; }
}

{
  "product_key": "consumer-qc",

  "version": "2026.06.03.1",

    "institution_id": "fi-123",
    "version": "2026.06.03.1",
    "product_id": "consumer-loan-qc",
    "rules": [],
    "derivations": [],
    "tables": {}
  },
  "active": false
}

docs.title: Scout HQ Endpoint
docs.text:
The SDK retrieves the authoring profile through Scout HQ:

GET /authoring-profiles/{profileKey}
X-Scout-Token: <fi-token>

Response shape:

{
  "institution": {
    "id": "fi-123",
    "name": "Example Bank"
  },
  "providers": {
    "anthropic": {
      "apiKey": "..."
    }
  },
  "profile": {
    "profileKey": "consumer-qc.consumer-loan-qc.policy-cel-authoring",
    "productKey": "consumer-qc",
    "workflowKey": "consumer-loan-qc",
    "bundleProductId": "consumer-loan-qc",
    "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6",
    "maxTokens": 16384,
    "systemPrompt": "...",
    "fieldDictionary": {},
    "referenceBundle": {},
    "oracleFixture": {},
    "validationPolicy": {},
    "version": "2026.06.03.1"
  }
}

docs.title: Detached Authoring Model
docs.text:
VisionFI Policy Analyzer is designed for partners who need to create rule bundles without using VisionFI CRM.

Partner Application
  -> VisionFI Policy Analyzer
      -> Scout HQ
          - FI token validation
          - institution identity
          - authoring profile
          - provider credentials
      -> Managed inference
          - policy PDFs/text
          - profile prompt and schema artifacts
      -> Local validation
      -> CRM-compatible rule-bundle wrapper

Scout HQ is the control plane for identity and authoring configuration. It is not the document processor in this flow.

docs.title: Scout HQ Responsibilities
docs.text:
Scout HQ provides:

  • FI token validation
  • Institution ID and institution name
  • Product/workflow-specific authoring profiles
  • Provider credentials associated with the FI token
  • Versioned schema artifacts used by the SDK

The same FI token used by Scout runtime flows can retrieve authoring profiles. For the initial partner flow, no product entitlement check is required; a valid token is sufficient.

docs.title: SDK Responsibilities
docs.text:
The SDK handles:

  • PDF and text source preparation
  • Authoring request construction
  • Managed inference calls from the partner environment
  • Evidence report parsing
  • Rule-bundle wrapper shaping
  • CEL bundle validation
  • Version consistency checks

The SDK uses the token-resolved institution.id from Scout HQ. The caller does not supply the institution ID.

docs.title: Authoring Profile Boundary
docs.text:
Authoring profiles are distinct from Scout Chat agents and Scout runtime workflows.

HQ object Purpose agents Scout Chat directives workflows Scout runtime workflow configuration rule_bundles Institution-specific executable CEL bundles authoring_profiles Instructions and schema artifacts for creating CEL bundles

This keeps Policy Analyzer from changing Scout Chat behavior or Scout runtime execution.

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
FI token
  -> Scout HQ
  -> institution identity + authoring profile + provider credentials

Policy PDFs / free-form text
  -> SDK
  -> managed inference provider
  -> SDK
  -> partner-owned storage

docs.title: Output Contract
docs.text:
The SDK returns the CRM-compatible wrapper:

{
  "product_key": "consumer-qc",
  "workflow_key": "consumer-loan-qc",
  "version": "2026.06.03.1",
  "bundle_json": {
    "institution_id": "fi-123",
    "version": "2026.06.03.1",
    "product_id": "consumer-loan-qc",
    "rules": [],
    "derivations": [],
    "tables": {}
  },
  "active": false
}

active remains false because promotion is a separate governance action.

docs.title: What does VisionFI Policy Analyzer do?
docs.text: It creates staged CEL rule bundles from policy documents and free-form policy text. The output is compatible with the rule-bundle wrapper shape used by VisionFI CRM and Scout HQ.

docs.title: Is this the old policy readiness review package?
docs.text: No. The old readiness-review package produced a markdown review and draft InstitutionConfig. This new package produces an evidence report and a staged CEL rule-bundle wrapper.

docs.title: Does the partner need VisionFI CRM?
docs.text: No. The partner application owns document collection, bundle storage, review, and later Scout HQ integration.

docs.title: What is an authoring profile?
docs.text:
An authoring profile is a Scout HQ record for a specific product/workflow pair. It contains the authoring prompt, model settings, field dictionary, reference bundle, oracle fixture, and validation policy.

Example:

consumer-qc.consumer-loan-qc.policy-cel-authoring

docs.title: Can the SDK use the FI token?
docs.text: Yes. The SDK uses the FI token in the X-Scout-Token header to retrieve the authoring profile and provider credentials from Scout HQ.

docs.title: Are product entitlements required?
docs.text: Not in the initial version. Any valid FI token can retrieve an active authoring profile.

docs.title: Does Scout HQ receive the policy documents?
docs.text: No. Scout HQ receives the FI token and returns configuration. Policy documents and free-form text go directly from the partner environment to managed inference.

docs.title: What does the SDK return?
docs.text:
The SDK returns:

  • evidence report markdown
  • staged rule-bundle wrapper JSON
  • validation results
  • authoring profile metadata
  • token usage, when available

docs.title: Why is active false?
docs.text: Generated bundles are authoring output, not approved runtime configuration. The partner decides when a bundle is approved and later integrated with Scout HQ.

docs.title: Who stores the bundle?
docs.text: The partner stores it. Scout HQ integration comes later.

docs.title: What is the NuGet package ID?
docs.text:
The package ID is:

VisionFI.PolicyAnalyzer

The package file for version 0.1.0 is:

VisionFI.PolicyAnalyzer.0.1.0.nupkg

The current public C# namespace remains:

using VisionFI.Scout.Authoring;

docs.title: Can the SDK accept free-form text?
docs.text: Yes. The source list can include PDFs and text inputs.

docs.title: Can it run in ASP.NET?
docs.text: Yes. The client can be registered with dependency injection and called from controllers, background jobs, or internal workflow services.

docs.title: What platforms are targeted?
docs.text: Windows, macOS, and Linux on-device support are assumed for the package direction.

docs.title: The authoring profile returns 404
docs.text: Confirm the profile key is correct and that the profile is active in Scout HQ seed/config data.

docs.title: The request is unauthorized
docs.text:
Confirm the FI token is active and sent as:

X-Scout-Token: <fi-token>

docs.title: The bundle fails validation
docs.text: The evidence report should explain blockers or ambiguous policy language. CEL validation errors usually mean the generated expression does not compile or references a field path outside the profile's field dictionary.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide shows the partner-facing flow for VisionFI Policy Analyzer.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• .NET 9.0+
  • Scout HQ base URL
  • FI token issued by Scout HQ
  • Network access from the partner environment to Scout HQ and the configured managed inference provider

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Package ID:

VisionFI.PolicyAnalyzer

Current package file:

VisionFI.PolicyAnalyzer.0.1.0.nupkg
NuGet CLIPackageReference 
dotnet add package VisionFI.PolicyAnalyzer --version 0.1.0

<PackageReference Include="VisionFI.PolicyAnalyzer" Version="0.1.0" />

The package ID is VisionFI.PolicyAnalyzer. The current public C# namespace is VisionFI.Scout.Authoring.

For temporary file-based distribution, place the .nupkg in a local folder and add that folder as a NuGet source:

dotnet nuget add source ./nuget-local --name VisionFI-Local
dotnet add package VisionFI.PolicyAnalyzer --version 0.1.0 --source ./nuget-local

When hosted by the VisionFI downloads portal, the stable download ID is expected to be:

nuget-policy-analyzer

docs.title: Author a Rule Bundle
What The SDK Does
docs.text:
The SDK:

  1. Calls Scout HQ with the FI token.
  2. Retrieves the requested authoring profile.
  3. Uses the token-resolved institution ID when shaping the bundle.
  4. Sends source material directly to managed inference.
  5. Forces wrapper and nested bundle version consistency.
  6. Validates the CEL bundle before returning it.

Scout HQ does not receive the policy PDF or free-form policy text.

docs.title: Authoring Profile
docs.text:
An authoring profile is specific to one product/workflow pair:

consumer-qc.consumer-loan-qc.policy-cel-authoring

The profile provides:

Field Purpose productKey Wrapper product_key workflowKey Wrapper workflow_key bundleProductId Nested bundle_json.product_id systemPrompt Authoring instructions fieldDictionary Valid pkg.* paths referenceBundle Known-good bundle shape oracleFixture Validation fixture for path linting validationPolicy Compile/path-lint requirements

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
AuthorRuleBundleResult contains:

Property Description EvidenceReportMarkdown Source-grounded explanation of what can and cannot become deterministic rules RuleBundleWrapperJson CRM/HQ-compatible staged rule-bundle wrapper Validation Local validation result, including CEL compile and field-path checks ProfileVersion Authoring profile version used InputTokens / OutputTokens Token usage, when returned by the provider

docs.title: Storage And Approval
docs.text: The partner owns storage, review, approval, and later Scout HQ integration. The SDK returns active: false because generated bundles are staged authoring output, not automatically approved runtime configuration.

docs.title: Core Boundary
docs.text:
Scout HQ does not receive policy PDFs, checklist documents, free-form policy text, or generated rule-bundle results in the detached authoring flow.

Scout HQ receives only the FI token and returns:

  • institution identity
  • authoring profile
  • provider credentials configured for that FI token

docs.title: What Leaves The Partner Environment
docs.text:
Destination Data Sent Scout HQ FI token only Managed inference provider Policy PDFs/text and authoring prompt VisionFI CRM Nothing

The partner application remains responsible for storage, approval, audit records, and later Scout HQ integration of the generated bundle.

docs.title: FI Token
docs.text:
The FI token authenticates the institution. The SDK uses it to retrieve:

  • institution.id
  • institution.name
  • authoring profile content
  • provider credentials

For the initial version, any valid FI token can retrieve an active authoring profile. Product entitlement checks can be added later without changing the SDK output contract.

docs.title: Provider Credentials
docs.text:
The FI token can return provider credentials, including an Anthropic API key. The SDK uses those credentials to call managed inference directly from the partner environment.

Partners should treat provider credentials as sensitive operational secrets:

  • do not log them
  • do not persist them outside approved secret storage
  • do not include them in support bundles or telemetry

docs.title: Document Handling
docs.text: The SDK should process source files in memory where practical. If the partner application persists documents or generated bundles, that storage is governed by the partner's own controls.

docs.title: Generated Bundle Status
docs.text:
Generated bundles are staged output. The SDK returns:

"active": false

That prevents authoring from being confused with approval. Promotion or activation remains a separate governance step.

docs.title: Audit Considerations
docs.text:
Partners should record:

  • authoring profile key and version
  • bundle version
  • source document names
  • timestamp
  • validation result
  • user or service principal that requested authoring

Do not log source document content, provider credentials, FI tokens, or PII.
